ana: quick heads-up — hosted->private fallbacks broke for a customer: dedicated runtime rejected payload with "unknown field: embeds"

tom: that smells like envelope drift. did the probe manifest show any `envelope_capabilities`?

ana: probe showed only `core_v1`. hosted recently started shipping `embeds` in responses.

liz: we have three levers here: 1) insist on capability handshake (strict), 2) add a control-plane translator (translate), 3) make runtimes permissive (lenient).

ryan: strict is safest long-term but risky for air-gapped/private installs. translate is pragmatic but centralizes complexity.

ana: proposal: hybrid approach — require a capability bit `envelope_embeds` going forward, but for a transition window hosting will attempt translation and set header `X-Envelope-Translated: 1`. if translation fails, respond 409 + body {code: "upgrade_required"}.

tom: agree. add feature-flag per-tenant so we can kill translation if it spikes latency. also add metric `envelope_translated_ratio` and alert >2%.

liz: translation must never mutate opaque blobs (signed tokens). copy-as-is, abort if validation would need re-signing. document that clearly in migration notes.

ana: ops action: publish a tiny shim lib `envelope-normalizer` for private runtimes that maps `embeds`<->`attachments` for old installs. include probe tests.

ryan: will draft RFC with example probe fields: `ProbeResponse.capabilities = ["core_v1", "envelope_embeds"]`, `FallbackPolicy = translate|reject`. will add unit + perf tests.

ops-bot: probe-job 999 completed on staging at 2026-03-25T11:02:00Z :white_check_mark:

ana: thanks — ping eng-arch when RFC posted. add rollback plan if translation P50 increases by >20ms. :thumbsup:
